# FEATURE: Inline HTML and Autolinks

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20260815 V1 |
| Description | Parse URI and email autolinks and preserve valid inline raw HTML. |
| Depends On  | FEATURE-Inline-Links.md |
| Provides    | URI autolinks, email autolinks, inline raw HTML |
| Consumes    | links and images, emphasis inline nodes, code spans |

## Questions

- None.

## Intent

The inline parser recognizes absolute URI and email autolinks enclosed in angle brackets and preserves valid raw HTML tags, comments, processing instructions, declarations, and CDATA sections. These constructs take precedence over emphasis and link grouping where required by CommonMark 0.31.2.

## Behavior

- Accept URI schemes of two to thirty-two ASCII characters followed by a colon.
- Accept valid HTML5-style email autolinks and render them with `mailto:` destinations.
- Preserve valid HTML tags and attributes without Markdown interpretation inside the tag.
- Preserve comments, processing instructions, declarations, and CDATA sections.
- Reject malformed tags and autolinks as literal text.
- Apply URL escaping to autolink destinations while preserving visible labels.
- Keep code spans, HTML tags, and autolinks ahead of emphasis parsing.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC inline-autolinks ===
Intent: The implementation passes the authoritative CommonMark autolink examples owned by this story.
Suite: scoped

import subprocess
import sys

result = subprocess.run(
    [
        sys.executable,
        "sources/spec_tests.py",
        "--spec",
        "sources/spec.txt",
        "--program",
        "./commonmark",
        "--pattern",
        r"^Autolinks$",
    ],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
=== END AC inline-autolinks ===

=== AC inline-raw-html ===
Intent: The implementation passes the authoritative CommonMark raw HTML examples owned by this story.
Suite: scoped

import subprocess
import sys

result = subprocess.run(
    [
        sys.executable,
        "sources/spec_tests.py",
        "--spec",
        "sources/spec.txt",
        "--program",
        "./commonmark",
        "--pattern",
        r"^Raw HTML$",
    ],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
=== END AC inline-raw-html ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- Do not use a public Markdown implementation.
- Do not parse malformed autolinks or HTML tags as valid structure.
- Do not invoke `full_test.sh` from scoped checks.

=== END ARTIFACT ===
=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-HTML-Renderer.md ===
# FEATURE: HTML Renderer

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20260815 V1 |
| Description | Render the complete parsed document as CommonMark-compatible HTML. |
| Depends On  | FEATURE-Inline-HTML-Autolinks.md |
| Provides    | HTML renderer |
| Consumes    | block nodes, inline nodes, list tightness, raw HTML nodes |

## Questions

- None.

## Intent

The renderer converts the completed block and inline tree into the HTML representation required by the supplied CommonMark 0.31.2 examples.

## Behavior

- Render paragraphs, headings, thematic breaks, code blocks, block quotes, lists, and list items.
- Render emphasis, strong emphasis, links, images, code spans, breaks, autolinks, entities, and raw HTML.
- Escape text, code content, attribute values, destinations, and titles according to the conformance examples.
- Preserve raw HTML nodes without escaping their markup.
- Render ordered-list start attributes and omit paragraph tags in tight lists.
- Emit the standard CommonMark HTML tag and whitespace conventions.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC renderer-conformance ===
Intent: The renderer passes the authoritative conformance examples covering the implemented rendered surface.
Suite: scoped

import subprocess
import sys

result = subprocess.run(
    [
        sys.executable,
        "sources/spec_tests.py",
        "--spec",
        "sources/spec.txt",
        "--program",
        "./commonmark",
        "--pattern",
        r"^(Thematic breaks|ATX headings|Setext headings|Indented code blocks|Fenced code blocks|HTML blocks|Block quotes|List items|Lists|Backslash escapes|Entity and numeric character references|Code spans|Emphasis and strong emphasis|Links|Images|Autolinks|Raw HTML|Hard line breaks|Soft line breaks)$",
    ],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
=== END AC renderer-conformance ===

=== AC renderer-processes-document ===
Intent: The renderer produces a nonempty HTML document for a valid Markdown document.
Suite: scoped

import subprocess

source = "# renderer\n"
result = subprocess.run(
    ["./commonmark"],
    input=source,
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr, file=__import__("sys").stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
assert result.stdout
=== END AC renderer-processes-document ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- Do not hand-code expectations that duplicate the authoritative conformance suite.
- Do not escape raw HTML nodes as ordinary text.
- Do not invoke `full_test.sh` from this story.

=== END ARTIFACT ===

# FEATURE: CLI Executable

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20260815 V1 |
| Description | Provide the UTF-8 standard-input/standard-output parser executable. |
| Depends On  | FEATURE-HTML-Renderer.md |
| Provides    | commonmark stdin/stdout executable |
| Consumes    | HTML renderer |

## Questions

- None.

## Intent

The executable provides the product boundary: it reads UTF-8 Markdown from standard input, renders it, and writes HTML to standard output without requiring a public Markdown runtime dependency.

## Behavior

- Consume all Markdown from standard input.
- Decode UTF-8 input and emit UTF-8 HTML on standard output.
- Preserve the adapter-compatible process contract used by `sources/cmark.py`.
- Write diagnostics to standard error when a process-level failure occurs.
- Return zero for successfully processed documents and nonzero for unrecoverable process failures.
- Avoid importing or invoking a public Markdown implementation.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC cli-stdin-stdout ===
Intent: The executable accepts Markdown on standard input and returns successful HTML output on standard output.

import subprocess

source = "plain text\n"
result = subprocess.run(
    ["./commonmark"],
    input=source,
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr, file=__import__("sys").stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
assert result.stdout
=== END AC cli-stdin-stdout ===

=== AC cli-utf8 ===
Intent: The executable accepts UTF-8 Markdown and emits UTF-8 output without a decoding failure.
Encoding: utf-8

import subprocess

source = "Unicode: café\n"
result = subprocess.run(
    ["./commonmark"],
    input=source,
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    encoding="utf-8",
)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr, file=__import__("sys").stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
assert result.stdout
=== END AC cli-utf8 ===

=== AC cli-empty-input ===
Intent: The executable completes successfully for an empty standard-input document.

import subprocess

result = subprocess.run(
    ["./commonmark"],
    input="",
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr, file=__import__("sys").stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
=== END AC cli-empty-input ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- Preserve the standard-input/standard-output contract.
- Do not require command-line arguments for ordinary conversion.
- Do not use a public Markdown implementation at runtime.

=== END ARTIFACT ===
=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-CLI-Boundaries.md ===
# FEATURE: CLI Boundary Handling

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20260815 V1 |
| Description | Handle malformed, empty, unclosed, and arbitrary Unicode input safely. |
| Depends On  | FEATURE-CLI-Executable.md |
| Provides    | safe malformed-input handling |
| Consumes    | commonmark stdin/stdout executable |

## Questions

- None.

## Intent

The parser and executable remain deterministic and non-crashing when input contains incomplete constructs, invalid syntax, empty documents, NUL characters, arbitrary Unicode, or deeply nested valid structures.

## Behavior

- Treat unclosed fenced code blocks and inline constructs according to CommonMark end-of-document rules.
- Preserve invalid syntax as literal content where the specification requires.
- Replace every U+0000 input character with U+FFFD.
- Accept arbitrary Unicode source text and emit valid UTF-8.
- Complete safely on empty input and documents containing only blank lines.
- Avoid unbounded recursion or delimiter failures on nested constructs.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC boundaries-unclosed ===
Intent: The executable safely processes unclosed and invalid CommonMark constructs.

import subprocess

source = "```\nunclosed\n"
result = subprocess.run(
    ["./commonmark"],
    input=source,
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr, file=__import__("sys").stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
=== END AC boundaries-unclosed ===

=== AC boundaries-nul ===
Intent: The executable accepts NUL-containing Markdown without a process failure and emits UTF-8 output.

import subprocess

source = "before\x00after\n"
result = subprocess.run(
    ["./commonmark"],
    input=source,
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    encoding="utf-8",
)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr, file=__import__("sys").stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
assert result.stdout
=== END AC boundaries-nul ===

=== AC boundaries-conformance ===
Intent: The implementation passes the authoritative bounded conformance examples relevant to malformed and unclosed input.
Suite: scoped

import subprocess
import sys

result = subprocess.run(
    [
        sys.executable,
        "sources/spec_tests.py",
        "--spec",
        "sources/spec.txt",
        "--program",
        "./commonmark",
        "--pattern",
        r"^(Fenced code blocks|Code spans|Links|Images|Raw HTML)$",
    ],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
=== END AC boundaries-conformance ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- Never crash on incomplete constructs or empty input.
- Replace U+0000 with U+FFFD before rendering.
- Do not invoke `full_test.sh` from scoped checks.

=== END ARTIFACT ===
=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Verification-Scoped.md ===
# FEATURE: Scoped Verification

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20260815 V1 |
| Description | Stage conformance assets and provide bounded specification-section checks. |
| Depends On  | FEATURE-CLI-Executable.md |
| Provides    | scoped conformance verification |
| Consumes    | commonmark stdin/stdout executable |

## Questions

- None.

## Verification Contract

The build environment stages the normative specification and its test helpers at:

- `sources/spec.txt`
- `sources/spec_tests.py`
- `sources/cmark.py`
- `sources/normalize.py`

Scoped verification invokes `spec_tests.py` with explicit `--pattern` or `--number` selectors. It must never invoke `full_test.sh`; the unfiltered suite is reserved for `FEATURE-Verification-Full.md`.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC scoped-section ===
Intent: A selected CommonMark specification section executes successfully against the completed executable.
Suite: scoped

import subprocess
import sys

result = subprocess.run(
    [
        sys.executable,
        "sources/spec_tests.py",
        "--spec",
        "sources/spec.txt",
        "--program",
        "./commonmark",
        "--pattern",
        r"^ATX headings$",
    ],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
=== END AC scoped-section ===

=== AC scoped-example ===
Intent: A single explicitly selected CommonMark example executes successfully against the completed executable.
Suite: scoped

import subprocess
import sys

result = subprocess.run(
    [
        sys.executable,
        "sources/spec_tests.py",
        "--spec",
        "sources/spec.txt",
        "--program",
        "./commonmark",
        "--number",
        "1",
    ],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
=== END AC scoped-example ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- Use explicit specification section or example selectors for every scoped check.
- Never invoke `full_test.sh` from scoped verification.
- Treat the conformance runner's exit status as the verdict; do not assert on printed tallies.
- Do not modify the staged conformance assets.

=== END ARTIFACT ===
